results.title: Diet Quality and Risk of Bladder Cancer in the Multiethnic Cohort Study.
results.reason: This prospective cohort study directly evaluated dietary DASH scores in relation to incident invasive bladder cancer and reported sex-specific adjusted hazard ratios.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest DASH score quintile
extraction.timing: Baseline dietary assessment, 1993–1996, with follow-up through 31 December 2017; mean follow-up 19.2 years
extraction.population: African American, Japanese American, Latino, Native Hawaiian, and non-Hispanic White Multiethnic Cohort participants aged 45–75 years
extraction.smoking_status: Mixed; never, former, and current smokers included with comprehensive smoking adjustment

effect_size.excerpt: lowest diet quality score quintile, HRs (95% CIs) in men was 1.08 (0.86-1.36) for HEI-2015, 1.05 (0.84-1.30) for AHEI-2010, 1.01 (0.80-1.27) for aMED, 1.13 (0.90-1.41) for DASH, and 0.96 (0.76-1.21) for DII®, whereas the corresponding HRs for women were 0.75 (0.53-1.07), 0.64 (0.45-0.92), 0.60 (0.40-0.88), 0.66 (0.46-0.95), and 0.63 (0.43-0.90) with all p values for trend <0.05. The inverse association found in women did not vary by smoking status or race and ethnicity.

results.title: Dietary patterns, polygenic risk, and kidney cancer incidence: a UK Biobank cohort study.
results.reason: This prospective UK Biobank cohort study directly evaluates dietary DASH adherence in relation to incident kidney cancer using Cox regression.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest DASH score quartile (Q4) versus lowest DASH score quartile (Q1)
extraction.timing: Dietary intake assessed at baseline in 2009–2012; participants were followed until kidney cancer diagnosis, death, or 31 October 2022, with a median follow-up of 11.44 years.

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a prospective cohort study involving 113,594 participants from the UK Biobank who completed at least two 24-hour dietary recalls, and adherence to four dietary patterns (Alternate Mediterranean Index (aMED), Alternative Healthy Eating Index 2010 (AHEI), dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH), and dietary inflammatory index (DII)) was assessed.

cases.excerpt: During a median follow-up of 11.44 years, 425 participants developed kidney cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Higher aMED (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.94) and DASH (HR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90) were associated with reduced risk of kidney cancer, while higher DII was associated with increased risk (HR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79). Moreover, participants with high genetic risk combined with low aMED, AHEI and DASH scores or high DII score presented the highest kidney cancer risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Higher aMED (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.94) and DASH (HR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90) were associated with reduced risk of kidney cancer, while higher DII was associated with increased risk (HR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79).
